messages:
Jess (Support): Heads-up — Marketly escalated. They see a bunch of streaming calls billed as 5xx even though their client reports a local disconnect. Customer claims ~3-5% of streams end with a client-side broken pipe, but our logs show 502/5xx and they get charged.
Jess (Support): Sample from customer:
```
Client error: ConnectionResetError: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer
Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d4e
Stream: /v1/streams/generate
````
Tyler (Eng): Thanks — can you upload a few full gateway logs (proxy + runtime) for those request IDs? We need the exact upstream status and bytes_sent. 502 could be a real runtime failure or our gateway marking a client abort as 5xx.
Jess (Support): Uploaded two snippets to the ticket with those IDs. Quick paste here:
```
proxy.log: time=2026-03-10T14:12:05Z req=r-0a1b2c4 upstream_status=502 bytes_sent=1024 client_err=ECONNRESET
runtime.log: time=2026-03-10T14:12:05Z req=r-0a1b2c4 handler=stream write_error=broken_pipe
```
Maria (SRE): The `bytes_sent=1024` is key — we actually sent some bytes. Kernel returns EPIPE when user closes connection mid-chunk. Historically some gateways labeled these as 5xx because the upstream handler returned an error on write. But we prefer classifying them as client aborts (499-like).
Tyler (Eng): Right, if the runtime returned an error due to EPIPE we currently bubble that up as a 5xx downstream. Easy to reproduce with a short script that opens stream then closes socket. Jess, can you ask Marketly for a repro script or try this snippet?
Jess (Support): I reproduced locally with their python snippet. Repro steps in ticket and trimmed here:
```bash
# start request, close after first chunk
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":100}' & sleep 0.2; pkill -f curl
```
Or python: 
```python
import requests, time, sys
r = requests.post(url, stream=True, headers=headers, data=data)
for i, chunk in enumerate(r.iter_content(chunk_size=1024)):
    print('got', len(chunk))
    if i==0:
        r.close()  # simulate abrupt client close
        break
```
Tyler (Eng): Reproduced. On our side, runtime hits write->EPIPE, logs write_error and returns an error to the http layer. The proxy sees upstream failure and emits 502 which is then counted as a 5xx.
Maria (SRE): Possible fixes: 1) Treat write errors caused by client resets after partial body as client-abort in the proxy layer (map to 499) 2) Change runtime to swallow EPIPE and return 200 with partial body/no error when appropriate 3) Add a post-hoc metric correction for billing (exclude these request-ids).
Jess (Support): Marketly asked for immediate billing relief for the impacted request-ids. I listed r-0a1b2c3d4e and r-7f8g9h0i1j in the ticket. Can finance do manual credit while engineering investigates?
Tyler (Eng): We should avoid manual credits if we can fix classification quickly. I'll try a proxy patch that detects upstream write failures where bytes_sent>0 and client reported ECONNRESET and map to 499/CLIENT_ABORT for metrics only. Canary on eng-runtime tomorrow.
Maria (SRE): Also add an option to collect a short pcap or tcpdump for a sample — kernel-level timing would confirm FIN vs RST. Asking Marketly if they can run tcpdump.
OpsBot: @oncall EngRuntime assigned: @Tyler (Eng) to investigate. Ticket #INC-8059 created.
Tyler (Eng): I'll post a short PR with tests that simulate the `r.close()` behavior and the expected metric mapping. If QA passes, we'll roll canary to 10% traffic, monitor token-billing/5xx counters.
Jess (Support): Thanks. I told Marketly the action plan and that we'll follow up within 48h. Also asked them to enable `X-Redwood-Debug: 1` for a few calls and to share more request IDs if they see more.
Marketly Support: Appreciate the quick response. We'll try to capture tcpdump and drop a few more request IDs in the ticket.
Tyler (Eng): Quick note for the runbook: when bytes_sent>0 and upstream returned write error due to EPIPE, treat as CLIENT_ABORT in metrics. Edgecase: if runtime hasn't flushed headers (no headers_sent) then keep 5xx. We'll add that logic.
Maria (SRE): Add unit tests that assert classification for partial-body abort vs runtime crash. Also add a dashboard row to show "partial-send client-aborts" so we can track frequency.
Jess (Support): I'll loop back with Marketly after patch canary. Marking this thread as pinned to the ticket.
Tyler (Eng): Assigned to me — will update thread when PR is opened.
Jess (Support): Thanks all :thumbsup:
